html: The Copuces were a small Chichimec people of the hills of today's Guanajuato and San Luis Potosí in central Mexico, on the northern edge of farming Mesoamerica. Little is recorded about them beyond their name. Spanish sources count them as one of the bands of the Guamares, hunting and gathering peoples who fought the Spanish hard in the Chichimeca War of about 1550 to 1590, alongside the Guachichil. After the war they were settled in missions and towns and absorbed into the society of New Spain.
